context.title: League of Women Voters of California — November 3, 2026 California general election endorsements

of.name: League of Women Voters of California

subject.title: California — Proposition 1 (Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs)

positions.statement: Public subsidy is necessary to provide safe and stable housing for households at the lowest incomes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 2 (Increases State's Rainy Day Fund)

positions.statement: Proposition 2 will allow California to save more money during strong economic years so it can protect schools and other essential services when revenues fall.

subject.title: California — Proposition 3 (Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes)

positions.statement: The League strongly supports the measure because it protects vital services, helps California weather economic downturns, and keeps the state’s tax system fair.

subject.title: California — Proposition 4 (Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns)

positions.statement: Prop 4 gives every California community the freedom to build elections where voters have more power and wealthy donors and special interests have less.

subject.title: California — Proposition 5 (Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers)

positions.statement: Prop 5 restores the recall to its proper purpose: deciding whether an official should remain in office.

subject.title: California — Proposition 37 (Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes)

positions.statement: California needs homeownership programs that lower families’ total costs, confront racial barriers to building wealth, and support strong communities. Prop 37 does not meet that test.

subject.title: California — Proposition 38 (Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research)

positions.statement: Medical research can save lives, but Prop 38 is the wrong way to fund it.

subject.title: California — Proposition 39 (Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification)

positions.statement: Don’t let President Trump and right-wing billionaires decide whose vote counts.

subject.title: California — Proposition 40 (Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers)

positions.statement: Because we have strong positions on both sides of this measure, the League takes a neutral position on Prop 40.

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.statement: Prop 41 would put revenue from new state taxes under the Gann Limit’s rigid constitutional spending cap, making it harder to fund essential services and respond to changing needs.

subject.title: California — Proposition 42 (Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes)

positions.statement: Prop 42 would lock broad new restrictions on state taxing power into the California Constitution, limiting California’s ability to respond to future needs.

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.statement: A simple majority keeps these decisions with most voters and gives communities more flexibility to respond to changing needs.

subject.title: California — Proposition 44 (Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services)

positions.statement: A rule intended to direct more money to patient care should not put the safety net itself at risk.

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.statement: But the process overhaul of CEQA proposed by Prop 45 goes too far.
